# Glance

> Ask an open vision-language model typed questions about an image (yes/no, pick-one, rating) and get probabilities back,
> on your own machine. The answer is read from the logits of one forward pass of a frozen open model (Qwen3-VL-4B by
> default); nothing is generated or trained. Glance is a calibration and measurement harness, not a model.

Use it for private or offline image decisions, many questions per image, probabilities to threshold on, and image-quality
rubrics you can fit from a few dozen images. Zero-shot, pooled over three sets of fresh photographs, the open 4B model is level with the
best hosted models on coarse pick-one questions and about two points behind the best (both Gemini models) on yes/no; on exact rating levels a cheap hosted model (Gemini 3.1
Flash-Lite, 0.763) is ahead zero-shot (0.669), about level once Glance has seen 16 unlabeled images of the rubric (0.758), and
behind after 32 labels (0.857). Know its limits: it confuses mirror-image diagonal directions, misjudges relative size, slips
when counting eight objects, and on rubrics that are not image quality (tilt, how much of a subject is cut off) even a 300-label
fit reaches only 0.55. For image-quality scoring alone, a small trained quality model or hand-built features do as well or better.

- README (install, usage, scorecard): README.md in the repository
- Operating guide for coding agents: AGENTS.md in the repository
- Every claim with evidence and caveats: docs/CLAIMS.md
- Results, generated from result files: docs/paper/RESULTS_ZEROSHOT.md, results/lab/matrix.md
- Pre-registration notebook: lab/NOTES.md
